images.title: Everything cancels, so 2⁰ = 1
images.purpose: Shows 2⁴ ÷ 2⁴ with all four factors cancelling, leaving 1, and the rule giving 2⁰, so 2⁰ = 1.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A fraction layout of circles with strike lines, and two short lines of working to its right.
images.exact_structure: Above a dark horizontal fraction line, a row of four equal plain teal (#0072B2) circles labelled 2⁴ at the left; below it, a row of four equal plain teal circles labelled 2⁴ at the left, each under one top circle. A small key reads each circle = 2. Each of the 8 circles has one grey (#6B7280) diagonal strike line. To the right, stacked: 16 ÷ 16 = 1, then 4 − 4 = 0, then in reddish purple (#CC79A7) the larger label 2⁰ = 1. Exactly 8 circles. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A power with exponent 0 is 1, so that the division rule keeps working.
images.description: Shows 2⁴ ÷ 2⁴ with all four factors cancelling, leaving 1, and the rule giving 2⁰, so 2⁰ = 1.
images.context: 2⁴ ÷ 2⁴ = 1 and also 2 to the power 4 − 4 = 2 to the power 0.

image_decisions.why: Seeing every factor cancel to 1 is the reason the zero exponent is defined as 1.
